patients.summary: 58-year-old library assistant on disability with seropositive RA complicated by Felty syndrome (chronic neutropenia, splenomegaly), steroid-induced osteoporosis and chronic fatigue, joined 2021. Two cellulitis episodes and a pneumonia in 2026 led to a June 2026 admission and scheduled twice-weekly filgrastim; a follow-up CBC is pending today.

documents.title: New Patient Intake Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is Patricia Kelleher, 53, asking to become a patient. Her previous doctor retired this summer and the office closed. Says she has rheumatoid arthritis and a blood count problem that two specialists follow, and she wanted a primary doctor who would actually pick up the phone between those visits. Membership explained, she wants to go ahead. Insurance verified (disability coverage). New patient visit booked 9/14 at 9:00. Records release signed electronically for the prior practice and for her hematology office. Asked her to bring all pill bottles and the injection she keeps in the fridge.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53F establishing care. Prior PCP retired; records requested.

RA: seropositive, diagnosed 2014 by an outside rheumatology group, who still see her about every 4-6 months. Methotrexate 20 mg every Sunday plus prednisone 5 mg each morning and folic acid on the other six days. Says the joints are "mostly behaving" - stiff for a while on waking, hands worst. Had both carpal tunnels released in 2016.

Blood counts: this spring hematology worked up her low white count and enlarged spleen - marrow biopsy in April, a needle sample of the spleen in May, both reportedly without anything malignant. Told it is Felty syndrome. Keeps filgrastim syringes at home and injects only when hematology calls with an ANC under 1000; has used it maybe twice. No infections this year.

Bones: DXA in 2019 showed osteoporosis, blamed on years of prednisone. Risedronate weekly since, calcium/D twice a day. No fractures.

Fatigue: carries a chronic fatigue diagnosis from her old office going back to roughly 2017. Cut her library hours because of it, now on disability. Sleeps 8 hours and still wakes tired. Mood ok.

Allergies: Bactrim - throat closed, ambulance (anaphylaxis). Ibuprofen - gastritis, told never to take NSAIDs.
FHx: mother RA. Maternal aunt lupus. Father T2DM and HTN.
SHx: never smoked, no alcohol since starting methotrexate. Lives alone. Part-time at a public library.

Exam: well-appearing, thin. Vitals as recorded. HEENT unremarkable, no oral ulcers. No cervical or axillary nodes. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft, spleen tip palpable below the left costal margin, nontender. Hands: MCP prominence and mild ulnar drift bilaterally, well-healed carpal tunnel scars, no warm or boggy joints today. No edema. Skin without rash or bruising.

A/P:
1. Seropositive RA - per rheumatology; will draw monitoring labs here when it helps her.
2. Felty syndrome - per hematology. CBC today for our own baseline.
3. Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis - continue risedronate and calcium/D; vitamin D level today. We will refill these.
4. Chronic fatigue syndrome - longstanding, pacing her activity.
5. Health maintenance - HCV and HIV screens today. Colonoscopy 2018 per her report, will confirm in records. Flu shot and pneumococcal vaccine next month. No live vaccines on her regimen.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Patricia - your labs from Tuesday are back. White count and neutrophils are low, about where your hematology notes say they usually run, and your hemoglobin is mildly low as before. Kidney and liver tests, which matter on methotrexate, are normal. Vitamin D is fine. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Nothing to change. I'll keep an eye on the trend along with your hematologist.

reports.text: Outside report, received 9/28/2021. Specimen: bone marrow core biopsy and aspirate, right posterior iliac crest. Core biopsy adequate. Cellularity is reduced for age. Myeloid series present with paucity of mature forms beyond the myelocyte stage, consistent with maturation arrest. Erythroid and megakaryocytic lineages present without dysplasia. No increase in blasts. No lymphoid aggregates or infiltrating process. Iron stores present.
reports.conclusion: Hypocellular marrow with myeloid maturation arrest. No evidence of malignancy.

reports.text: Outside report, received 9/28/2021. Specimen: fine-needle aspiration, spleen, ultrasound guided. Smears show a mixed population of small lymphocytes, scattered histiocytes and blood elements. No monoclonal population on flow cytometry. No granulomas. No malignant cells.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Outside report, received 9/28/2021. Indication: long-term glucocorticoid therapy. L1-L4 lumbar spine T-score -2.7. Left femoral neck T-score -2.4. Left total hip within the low bone mass range.

documents.title: Records from Prior Primary Care and Hematology
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received 41 pages from the prior primary care office and 18 pages from hematology. Scanned to chart.

Abstract (prior PCP): RA since 2014 per rheumatology. Chronic fatigue syndrome listed since 2017. Bilateral carpal tunnel release 2016. DXA 06/2019 osteoporosis, risedronate started 06/2019. Colonoscopy 03/2018 normal, repeat 10 years. Mammogram 08/2020 negative. Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Abstract (hematology): referred spring 2021 for neutropenia with splenomegaly. Marrow biopsy 04/2021 and splenic FNA 05/2021, benign. Assessment Felty syndrome. Filgrastim 300 mcg as needed for ANC <1000. Follow-up every 6 months.

Rheumatology notes not included - separate request faxed today.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for flu and pneumococcal vaccines per PCP. Afebrile, feels well. Allergies reviewed (sulfa antibiotics - anaphylaxis; ibuprofen). Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. PCV20 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 minutes, no reaction. Told her PCV20 covers her for pneumococcus, no further pneumococcal doses planned.

documents.title: Rheumatology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Visit date: 11/04/2021

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for taking over primary care for Ms. Kelleher, whom we follow for seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, diagnosed here in 2014 with strongly positive RF and anti-CCP and a synovial biopsy at the time showing pannus with plasma cell and lymphocyte infiltrates. Her course has been complicated by Felty syndrome, which hematology is managing.

Today she has about 45 minutes of morning stiffness. Exam shows fixed MCP changes in both hands without active synovitis; wrists and knees quiet.

Medications: methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, folic acid 1 mg daily except methotrexate day, risedronate 35 mg weekly, calcium carbonate/vitamin D3 twice daily, filgrastim 300 mcg as needed.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis); ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Plan: continue current regimen. CBC and CMP every 3 months; happy for these to be drawn at your office and copied to us. Return in 6 months.

Sincerely,
Rheumatology

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
6-month follow-up.

S: Feeling about the same. Energy is the usual limit - works three short shifts a week and rests after. Joint stiffness on waking, eases by mid-morning. No infections over the winter. Has not needed filgrastim since joining. Takes risedronate Saturday mornings without heartburn.

O: Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Spleen tip still palpable, nontender. Hands with chronic MCP changes, no synovitis. No bruising.

A/P:
- RA and Felty syndrome: stable, specialists following; March labs at her baseline.
- Osteoporosis: continue risedronate and calcium/D. DXA due 2023.
- Chronic fatigue: unchanged.
- Recombinant zoster vaccine dose 1 today (non-live, fine with methotrexate). Dose 2 in 2 months.

See me in the fall for her annual wellness visit.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Second recombinant zoster dose IM left deltoid. First dose in April gave her a tired, achy day afterward; warned it may repeat. Series now complete.

documents.title: Hematology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: hematology
documents.body:
Visit date: 07/12/2022

Re: Patricia Kelleher

Ms. Kelleher returns for routine follow-up of Felty syndrome. She reports no fevers, mouth sores or infections since her last visit and has not needed growth factor. Spleen palpable one fingerbreadth below the costal margin. Counts remain low but steady: WBC in the high 2s, ANC around 1.2-1.4, hemoglobin about 11, platelets in the 150s.

Current medicines: methotrexate 20 mg weekly, prednisone 5 mg daily, folic acid, risedronate, calcium/vitamin D, filgrastim 300 mcg SC as needed.
Allergies: sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim (anaphylaxis), ibuprofen (gastropathy).

Impression: Felty syndrome, stable neutropenia without infectious complications.
Plan: continue as-needed filgrastim for ANC <1000. Fever precautions reviewed. Return in 6 months with CBC.

Hematology & Oncology

reports.text: Liquid-based cervical cytology. Specimen adequate; transformation zone component present. No intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV not detected.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy; HPV negative.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial annual wellness visit.

Functional: independent at home, drives, still working part-time. No falls in the past year. Hearing and vision adequate with readers. Home safety reviewed; grab bar in shower already.
Cognition: normal recall and clock draw.
Mood: PHQ-2 negative.

Interval: no infections, no filgrastim use. Hematology in July unchanged. Rheumatology letter on file from November; she saw them again in May, says nothing changed.

Exam: as before. Spleen tip palpable. Hands with old RA changes, no active synovitis. Breast exam normal. Pelvic exam with speculum, Pap/HPV collected.

Plan / prevention:
- Pap with HPV today.
- Screening mammogram ordered (last 2020).
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal, next 2028.
- Flu and updated COVID shot next month.
- Labs: CBC, CMP for methotrexate, lipids.
- Continue current medicines. Advance directive discussed; she will think about a health care proxy and bring the form back.

documents.title: Pap and blood work
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your Pap and HPV test are both negative, so no repeat for 5 years. Cholesterol numbers are good. Blood counts are steady at your usual level and the liver and kidney tests are normal.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison 08/2020. Breasts are heterogeneously dense. No suspicious mass, calcifications or architectural distortion.

documents.title: Mammogram Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening mammogram negative. Letter sent by imaging center. Next screening in 1-2 years.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine R deltoid, bivalent COVID booster L deltoid. Tolerated. 15 minute wait done. Next flu shot due next autumn.

documents.title: Refill and a question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I need the calcium with D sent again, the pharmacy says no refills left. Also is it normal to be extra wiped out in the early dark months? I'm not sick, just more tired than summer. Thank you - Pat

documents.title: RE: Refill and a question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Calcium/D sent with a year of refills. A dip in energy over the winter is common with chronic fatigue, and nothing in your September labs suggests a new cause. If you get fevers, sore throat, or anything that feels like an infection, call us that day - with your counts we want to see you quickly. Otherwise we'll talk more in the spring.
